stories.title: Maersk confirms data breach as WhiteArmor ransomware demands $5 million
stories.summary: Maersk announced that a threat actor gained unauthorized access to a local legacy system inherited through an earlier acquisition and extracted data from it.

stories.title: N-able releases security hotfixes for zero-day vulnerabilities
stories.summary: N-able released hotfixes to address zero-day bugs affecting its N-central remote monitoring and management (RMM) platform, which were publicly disclosed over the weekend and forced it to take vulnerable hosted environments offline.

stories.title: Hackers Target N-central Zero-Days as N-able Rushes Patches
stories.summary: The malicious activity started shortly after a researcher dropped over 30 zero-days. N-able patched the unauthenticated ones.

stories.title: PTC Patches Critical Windchill and FlexPLM Flaw That Could Enable Remote Code Execution
stories.summary: PTC has released patches for a new critical vulnerability impacting Windchill and FlexPLM software that, if successfully exploited, could result in remote code execution. The security flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-126325, carries a CVSS v4 score of 9.2 out of a maximum of 10.0. stories.title: CISA flags Cisco BroadWorks flaw as actively exploited in attacks
stories.summary: The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned on Tuesday that hackers are now exploiting a high-severity Cisco BroadWorks vulnerability in attacks.

stories.title: Cisco BroadWorks and Openwave Flaws Actively Exploited Despite Available Patches
stories.summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) Tuesday added two security flaws impacting Cisco BroadWorks and Openwave Messaging Webtop Media Transcoder to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation. Details of the vulnerabilities are below - CVE-2026-20320 (CVSS score: 7.5) - An improper restriction of XML external entity

stories.title: Hackers plant GSocket on Linux servers for persistent access
stories.summary: Multiple threat actors are abusing GSocket, a legitimate open-source remote access tool, to maintain access to Linux servers even after patching the vulnerabilities exploited to gain initial access.

stories.title: eBPF Rootkits: Why Underground Actors Are Taking Notice
stories.summary: Linux eBPF rootkits can hide malicious activity and evade traditional detection methods without loading kernel modules. Flare reveals how these techniques are spreading through underground forums, where threat actors are sharing rootkit source code, tutorials, and exploits targeting Linux systems.
